subject: Onshore wipe evidence — proposed Annex wording and timeline
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Questions on onshore wipe timing & evidence for DPA Annex

Hi Rafael / Laura,

Thanks for sending the DPA redline earlier today. Our legal and security teams have two quick, concrete asks so we can sign the Annex:

1) Exact timing for onshore wipe from primary storage vs backups (they want an unambiguous timeline).
2) What form of proof/evidence will Redwood provide that a wipe occurred (e.g., signed manifest, SHA256 manifest, timestamped deletion logs, a certificate).

We attached a short vendor guidance doc that our InfoSec sent (vendor-erasure-reqs.pdf) to show the level of evidence they expect. We understand operational realities (snapshots, backups), so if you have a compromise proposal (e.g., tombstone + backup scrub window + certificate), that would be helpful.

Also, are you able to provide a short sample clause we can paste into the Annex rather than trying to draft from scratch? Our counsel prefers a single-line operational clause and a short schedule for timelines.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are aiming to get this wrapped before our board meeting next week.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health
[sara.patel@nimbushealth.com]

[Attachment: vendor-erasure-reqs.pdf (pdf)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Questions on onshore wipe timing & evidence for DPA Annex

Sara — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the vendor guidance. Pasting direct answers below and then a suggested Annex snippet in my follow-up.

Q1 — Timing (concise):
- Primary data deletion: within 7 calendar days of a validated customer request (records moved to tombstone state and removed from active replicas).
- Backup/secondary copies: best-effort scrub completed within 45 calendar days; operational backups are rotated/overwritten and subject to immutable snapshot windows.
- If expedited scrub is required for contract reasons, Redwood will provide a target expedited window (negotiated) and use prioritized scrub on affected shards.

Q2 — Evidence / proof (we can provide a combination):
- A machine-readable manifest listing affected object IDs and SHA256 digests (where applicable), with timestamps.
- An operator-signed wipe log (syslog entry with job ID, timestamp, operator idempotency token).
- A short “Erase Certificate” PDF: timestamped, signed by Redwood Security Ops, referencing the manifest/job ID.

We can attach our recommended evidence checklist and a draft Annex clause.

Next steps: I attached DPA_redline_v3.docx with inline suggestions and a one‑paragraph Annex sample. Also attaching a short erase-evidence-checklist.pdf that maps what we can deliver vs what is operationally unrealistic (e.g., immutable overwritten blocks).

Proposed compromise we typically use with enterprise customers: 7-day primary deletion + 45-day backup scrub, plus deliverables: manifest + erase certificate within 5 business days after scrub completion. If Nimbus requires the certificate earlier (post-tombstone), we can issue a preliminary confirmation that primary deletion completed and a final certificate after the backup scrub.

Happy to hop on a quick call if legal wants to walk through wording.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

[Attachments: DPA_redline_v3.docx (docx), erase-evidence-checklist.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Questions on onshore wipe timing & evidence for DPA Annex

Sara — quick follow up from our side with a practical compromise that has been accepted by other healthcare customers:

1) Operational timing: primary deletion within 7 days; backup scrub within 45 days. We can commit to exception handling for legal holds (see clause below).

2) Evidence: Redwood will provide — a) manifest (object IDs + hashes where applicable), b) operator-signed job log, c) final Erase Certificate PDF referencing job IDs and scrub completion timestamp. We can also provide the internal ticket ID for audit traceability.

3) Extra assurance: if Nimbus requires a notarized statement, we can include an optional 3rd-party attestation add-on (separate SOW).

Suggested playbook language to include in the Annex (short):
"Onshore-Wipe Annex (sample) — Redwood will move Customer Data to a tombstone state within 7 calendar days of a validated deletion request. Secondary and backup copies will be scrubbed per Redwood's backup rotation policies and completed within 45 calendar days. Upon completion of the scrub, Redwood will deliver a machine-readable manifest and a signed Erase Certificate referencing job IDs and timestamps. Legal holds requested by Customer will pause the scrub for affected datasets and will be handled according to the eDiscovery procedure set forth in Annex B."

If that wording looks good, Rafael will drop a plain-text snippet you can paste into your redline.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Annex sample & exact clause for paste-in

Sara — attaching a plain-text Annex snippet below you can paste directly into your DPA redline, plus the checklist we discussed. If Nimbus legal wants any edits to the language (shorter/longer), flag them and we’ll iterate quickly.

--- begin snippet ---
Annex X (Onshore Wipe and Erasure Evidence)
1. Deletion request processing: Redwood will validate and accept a Customer deletion request and place the relevant Customer Data into a tombstone state within seven (7) calendar days of validation.
2. Backup scrub: Redwood will complete a scrub of secondary and backup copies within forty-five (45) calendar days of the validated deletion request, subject to existing snapshot retention windows.
3. Evidence deliverables: Within five (5) business days following completion of the backup scrub, Redwood will deliver: (a) a machine-readable manifest identifying affected objects and hashes where applicable; (b) an operator-signed job log referencing internal job ID(s) and timestamps; and (c) a signed Erase Certificate PDF referencing the job ID(s) and manifest.
4. Legal holds: Any Customer notice of legal hold for specific datasets will pause the scrub for those datasets and be handled pursuant to the eDiscovery procedure set forth in Annex B.
--- end snippet ---

Next steps:
- I’ve uploaded the Annex snippet as onshore-wipe-annex-sample.txt to the Drive link below for your counsel to copy.
- If you confirm the compromise (7/45 + certificate), we’ll prepare a tracked-change DPA update and target signature next week.
